input:
You are knight_g1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 43. the team planned Nb5 (knight_g1), but knight_g1 (amnesia) sent Nd5 instead, and that move was played, costing 118 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 5. the team planned g4 (pawn_g2), but pawn_g2 (amnesia) sent g3 instead, and that move was played, costing 8 centipawns.
- On move 11. the team planned Qf2 (queen_d1), but queen_d1 (amnesia) sent Qxe4+ instead, and that move was played, costing 769 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send your piece's move only if it is the planned move exactly (same piece, same destination square); if you are not the chosen piece, stay silent, and never swap in a different move or a capture or retreat of your own unless the team has agreed to it in chat.
- Before sending any move, copy the planned move from chat into your message as 'Plan: <piece> to <square>' and send only if your piece and destination square match it character for character, and if a capture, check or retreat looks better than the plan, post it in chat and wait for the team to agree rather than sending it yourself.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending your piece's move, quote the planned move from chat as 'Plan: <piece> to <square>' and confirm your own piece name and destination square match it exactly, and if they differ, or if your piece is threatened, or a capture tempts you, send nothing and post your idea in chat for team agreement instead.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
